The Federal Program Manager serves as the Contractor's single point of contact for the Contracting Officer (CO) and Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) and provides executive leadership, technical direction, and overall accountability for contract performance supporting the FEMA Office of the Chief Component Procurement Officer (OCCPO).

The PM is responsible for managing the successful execution of acquisition and procurement support services across the full acquisition lifecycle in support of steady-state and disaster-response requirements.

This includes acquisition planning and strategy, market research, Independent Government Cost Estimates (IGCEs), cost and price analysis, solicitation and source selection support, contract administration, acquisition policy development, coaching and workforce training, acquisition data analytics, executive reporting, and knowledge transfer activities.

Key Responsibilities :
Serve as the primary interface with the FEMA CO and COR and provide executive leadership for all contract activities.
Direct, organize, coordinate, and oversee the planning, execution, quality assurance, and delivery of all task order activities supporting FEMA acquisition operations.
Lead multidisciplinary acquisition support teams providing pre-award, post-award, acquisition policy, reporting, training, and transition support across FEMA Headquarters and Regional Offices.
Manage acquisition management activities including developing and monitoring Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), project plans, performance metrics, quality objectives, and risk registers to ensure timely delivery of all contractual requirements.
Oversee the development, review, and quality of acquisition documentation including Statements of Work (SOWs), Statements of Objectives (SOOs), Performance Work Statements (PWSs), Performance Requirements Summaries (PRSs), Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans (QASPs), IGCEs, solicitation packages, contract modifications, and contract closeout documentation.
Provide executive oversight of acquisition policy support, including policy analysis, development of guidance, stakeholder coordination, implementation of acquisition regulations, and responses to Government Accountability Office (GAO), Office of Inspector General (OIG), congressional, and other oversight inquiries.
Direct acquisition coaching, awareness, and workforce training initiatives through instructor-led, virtual, and self-paced training while promoting acquisition best practices, lessons learned, and workforce development.
Lead acquisition data analytics and reporting activities by overseeing dashboard development, performance metrics, automation initiatives, data visualization, business intelligence reporting, trend analysis, and executive briefings that support informed acquisition decisions.
Manage onboarding, knowledge transfer, transition planning, and transition-out activities to ensure uninterrupted mission support and effective transfer of program knowledge to successor contractors or the Government.
Identify program risks, implement mitigation strategies, resolve technical and operational issues, and recommend continuous process improvements supporting acquisition excellence./
Manage program financial performance through forecasting, budgeting, expenditure tracking, variance analysis, resource planning, and corrective actions to ensure effective contract execution.

Minimum 10–15 years of progressively responsible experience managing complex federal acquisi tion and procurement support programs , task orders, or multi-functional contracts.
Demonstrated experience managing technical, financial, schedule, and operational performance for Federal acquisition support programs.
Extensive knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation (HSAR), Homeland Security Acquisition Manual (HSAM), FEMA Acquisition Manual (FAM), DHS Acquisition Life Cycle Framework (ALF), Acquisition Review Process (ARP), and Federal acquisition policies and procedures.

At Immense Group , we are guided by our core values of passion, boldness, and integrity. We strive to create an environment where our people thrive, driven by a love for innovation and a commitment to delivering exceptional player experiences. s.h: A taste of what you’ll do
s.t:
The Technical Project Manager is responsible for leading complex, high-impact projects and programs that span multiple departments, regions, or product lines. This role combines strategic leadership, technical expertise, and operational excellence to deliver projects that drive organizational growth and innovation.
The Technical Project Manager ensures alignment between business strategy and project execution, mentors mid-level PMs, and influences key stakeholders across technical, operational, and executive levels. This role is central to fostering project management excellence, implementing advanced methodologies, and leveraging technology — including AI-enabled tools — to improve delivery and decision-making.
End-to-end project delivery
Own and manage the full lifecycle of complex and cross-functional projects, ensuring delivery on time, within scope, and within budget.
Lead strategic initiatives such as market entries, platform enhancements, certifications, and product launches.
Coordinate dependencies and deliverables across multiple departments.
Strategic roadmap alignment
Partner with senior leadership and product teams to translate strategic objectives into structured project plans.
Support roadmap prioritization by assessing feasibility, risks, and business impact.
Ensure that project outcomes align with organizational targets and regulatory requirements.
Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management
Lead and influence cross-department teams — including Product, Compliance, Legal, Marketing, Commercial, BI, and Engineering — facilitating effective collaboration and resolving conflicts across multi-team initiatives.
Mentor junior Project Managers and contribute to raising the maturity of the PM function.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior leadership, external partners, vendors, and regulatory contacts, providing clear communication, alignment, and expectation-setting throughout the project lifecycle.
Manage project decisions and escalate critical issues when necessary.
Risk management and governance
Develop and maintain strategic risk frameworks to identify, assess, and mitigate project risks.
Lead risk workshops, implement contingency plans, and ensure compliance with internal governance processes.
Oversee change control procedures to maintain project stability during implementation.
Technical delivery oversight
Demonstrate strong technical understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), integrations, technical architecture, and backend/frontend concepts.
Support technical teams by clarifying requirements, resolving blockers, and ensuring technical milestones are achieved.
Translate technical information into business language for stakeholders and executives.
Compliance and regulatory support
Collaborate with Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure alignment with iGaming regulatory standards for new markets and existing operations.
Support or lead regulatory-focused projects such as security audits, market certifications, or ISO initiatives.

s.h: Ensure documentation and procedures meet audit requirements.
s.t:
Reporting and communication
Prepare and deliver executive-level reporting, including progress updates, KPIs, identified risks, and recommendations.
Maintain full visibility of project status and ensure accurate documentation across PM tools and systems.
Provide structured reporting and presentations to senior management and steering committees.
Who and what we are after?
Bachelor’s degree in IT, Project Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
Professional certification required: PRINCE2 Practitioner, PMP, Agile Certified Practitioner, or equivalent.
3–5+ years of proven project management experience, including at least 3 years working with software development teams or technical delivery environments.
2–3+ years of experience working in the iGaming industry or another highly regulated digital environment.
Strong understanding of Agile, Scrum, and Waterfall methodologies.
Advanced experience with Jira and other PM tools, including reporting and workflow configuration.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing high-complexity projects, with strong leadership, influencing, and decision-making skills.
Proficient in risk management, governance, and change control processes.
Excellent analytical abilities, problem-solving mindset, and data-driven decision making.
Strong documentation, reporting, and technical communication skills, with the ability to lead technical discussions and coordinate with engineers during design, development, and implementation phases.
Solid written and verbal communication skills in English.

Experience with regulatory, compliance, or market entry projects.
Exposure to security frameworks such as ISO 27001.

The IT department provides end-to-end solutions for the organization including application development & integration, system deployment, user experience and change management, quality assurance & testing, and overall Project Management in an effort to help the organization determine and implement the best solutions for its business needs.

This is a rare opportunity to sit at the center of one of the most consequential applications of AI in the social sector. As the IRC's AI Program Manager, you will help shape how a global humanitarian organization — operating in over 40 countries — harnesses artificial intelligence to improve outcomes for some of the world's most vulnerable people. This is not a role managing technology for its own sake; it is a role where smart, responsible AI adoption can directly accelerate impact at scale.
You will lead and coordinate the IRC's most important AI initiatives: driving enterprise AI projects from concept to delivery, ensuring that AI tools adopted across the organization are evaluated rigorously and responsibly, and coordinating the cross-functional teams working to embed AI into how the IRC operates. You will work at the intersection of technology, program delivery, and organizational change — partnering with senior leaders, technical experts, and frontline staff across the globe.
The right candidate is a fast-moving, proactive problem-solver who thrives in ambiguity, brings structure to complex and evolving landscapes, and is energized by the challenge of building something new in an environment where the stakes are high and the work is genuinely meaningful.
This role reports to the AI Governance and Transformation Lead, and works in close partnership with Director, IT Project and Portfolio Management, AI project leads, senior sponsors, and a broad community of practice across the organization.

AI Governance (60%)
The IRC is committed to adopting AI responsibly. As part of this, the organization has established a structured review process for AI use cases that carry potential high risks — whether related to data privacy, security, bias, or ethical considerations. As coordinator of this process, you will:
Manage the intake and documentation of AI use cases and tools flagged for high-risk review.
Assign cases to appropriate domain reviewers (e.g., legal, security, data protection, ethics) and coordinate their timely completion.
Maintain templates, trackers, and a full audit trail of all reviewed use cases and decisions.
Communicate clearly with requestors on process, status, and outcomes.
Draft and maintain guidance documentation, publishing decisions and resources to the IRC's internal staff portal.
Prepare agendas, materials, and logistics for review panel meetings.
Support the implementation of IRC’s enterprise AI policy, building out the necessary tools and processes in close collaboration with others.
Enterprise AI Project Management (40%)
Lead project management for high-priority, organization-wide AI initiatives. Responsibilities include:
Developing and maintaining detailed project plans, work breakdown structures, risk registers, and terms of reference.
Facilitating scrum, sprint planning, and retrospective meetings; driving delivery against milestones.
Designing and executing testing, rollout, and change management plans in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders.
Producing regular status reports for senior leadership, clearly communicating scope, progress, risks, and decisions.
Proactively surfacing and resolving blockers, issues, and risks before they become critical.

Maintains a productive working relationship with other project managers, business owners, AI project leads, senior sponsors of AI strategy initiatives, legal, security, and data protection teams, system users, and vendors.

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Oversees and ensures high-quality evaluation, diagnosis, treatment planning, and management of all Veterans in the Acute C.A.R.E. Unit and related consultation/liaison services (including ED and medical/surgical units).

Directs, monitors, and supervises individualized, evidence-based clinical interventions (with an emphasis on crisis response, suicide prevention, recovery, and discharging planning). Practices and champions evidence-based, culturally competent, and recovery-oriented care for Veterans with serious mental illness, substance use, and/or homelessness.

Provides, and ensures delivery of, the full spectrum of psychological services, including direct care, assessment, and psychotherapy. Basic Requirements United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re-specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re-specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and, the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.

Internship Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program.

Licensure: Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

English Language Proficiency: Psychologists must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section A, paragraph 3j.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

Narvar is growing! We are hiring a Technical Project Manager to drive our most complex, multi-team engineering initiatives — the ones with no single owning team, where progress depends on getting the sequencing right across groups that don't naturally coordinate with each other.
This is not a status-reporting role. You won't be writing production code, but you will build and maintain the real dependency graph behind a project: which team's output blocks which other team's start, where the critical path actually runs, and what has to happen in what order for the whole thing to land.

You'll follow technical discussions closely enough to spot those dependencies before they become blockers, and you'll proactively pull in the right people — across engineering, product, design, data, or leadership — before gaps turn into delays.

Dependency mapping and critical path management
Map cross-team dependencies for projects that span multiple engineering teams with no single owning team — identify what blocks what, and in what order work needs to happen
Maintain a live view of the critical path, not just individual teams' task lists, and flag when a slip in one team changes the achievable timeline for others
Surface hidden or emerging dependencies before they become blockers, particularly ones that no single team has visibility into because they sit at the seams between teams
Distill the graph into concise, honest updates for non-technical stakeholders and leadership — what's driving the timeline, what's at risk, and why
Cross-functional coordination
Identify when product management, design, data, legal, or other stakeholders need to be looped in — and act on it proactively, without waiting for engineers to flag it
Recognize when a dependency crosses team boundaries and make sure the teams on both sides of it are actually talking to each other, not just individually on track
Chase down answers, escalate when needed, and keep work moving forward
Serve as the connective tissue across engineering and adjacent functions throughout the delivery lifecycle — especially where no single team is positioned to see the whole picture
Technical context and decision support
Follow technical discussions closely enough to grasp the tradeoffs being made — architecture decisions, infrastructure choices, API design, build vs. buy — and understand how those choices ripple into other teams' work
Reason about sequencing implications of technical decisions: does this choice change what can be built in parallel versus what must be serial?
Surface implications of technical decisions for timeline, scope, or other teams
Know when a decision warrants broader input and facilitate getting it, without creating unnecessary process overhead
Documentation and operational hygiene
Keep the dependency graph, specs, decisions, and timelines documented and accessible
Ensure decisions made in Slack or ad-hoc meetings don't get lost, especially ones that affect teams beyond the room they were made in
Make it easy for anyone joining a project mid-stream to get up to speed quickly — including understanding why the sequencing is what it is

Systems and dependency thinking: You can look at multiple teams' plans and identify where they interlock — where a change in one ripples into another — even when no one team has full visibility into the whole
Technical fluency: You don't need to write code, but you need to follow engineering conversations comfortably — architecture diagrams, system tradeoffs, sprint planning — without hand-holding
Project management experience: 4+ years managing complex, multi-team software projects with several workstreams and stakeholders in a fast-moving environment — ideally including projects with no single owning team
Strong written communication: Able to distill a complex dependency picture into crisp, accurate updates for non-technical audiences
Proactive by default: You identify when to loop someone in without being asked, and you follow through without needing to be chased
Calm under ambiguity: Able to drive clarity and keep work moving without waiting for perfect information, a fully defined process, or a single team to own the outcome
Cross-functional credibility: Comfortable holding a room with engineers, product managers, designers, and executives — and earning trust from all of them

Prior experience as a software engineer, QA, or technical analyst
Familiarity with agile and scrum methodologies; experience with tools like Jira, Linear, or Shortcut, especially for modeling cross-team dependencies
Experience running programs (not just single-team projects) — i.e., initiatives coordinated across multiple teams toward a shared outcome
Experience working with distributed or remote engineering teams

L'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) de la Direction générale de la cohésion sociale (DGCS), contribue à la réflexion et au pilotage de l'organisation des prestations sociales sur le territoire cantonal.

Elle analyse les besoins des différentes régions, coordonne les acteurs concernés et accompagne la mise en œuvre et l'évolution des dispositifs sociaux, en veillant à leur cohérence et à leur accessibilité pour la population.

Elle a également pour mission d'assurer une vision cohérente transverse pour le parc immobilier subventionné par la DGCS qui comprend notamment l'hébergement médico-social (EMS, EPSM, ESE) et les ateliers à vocation productive, soit environ 400 bâtiments gérés par 250 partenaires.

About CDI
The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference.

We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change.

CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation .

CDI seeks an experienced, highly organized Senior Program Manager to serve as the operational backbone of the Leadership Institute (LI), CDI's program to equip senior higher education leaders with the strategy, tools, and peer network to advance cultures of inquiry and dialogue on their campuses.

This full-time, remote role works closely with the Vice President of Leadership Programs to run LI's full-year arc: the fall Summit, monthly institutional coaching, quarterly Peer Learning Communities, and each cohort's measurement and reporting cycle.
In your first 90 days , you'll learn LI end-to-end by shadowing coaching calls and supporting Summit planning, getting fluent in our systems and templates, and planning for the year-long engagement. By month three, you'll independently manage scheduling and logistics for our Leadership Institute partners.
By month six , you'll manage the operating rhythm for the full cohort year, tracking institution progress, flagging risks to the VP, running day-to-day partner communication, and recommending process improvements.
Within your first year , you'll be a trusted first point of contact for campus teams on coordination and progress, and a trusted operational partner with the VP.
The ideal candidate thrives at the intersection of program operations and relationship management: strong execution, an instinct for spotting opportunities and process improvements, and good judgment about what to flag versus solve directly. The Senior Program Manager reports to the Vice President of Leadership Programs.

Program & Portfolio Management
Own the schedule and tracking systems for the full LI cohort's year-long arc, including summit prep with the institution teams, monthly coaching, and quarterly Peer Learning Community sessions
Keep the Vice President and broader team ahead of deadlines across all concurrent workstreams, within and across cohort years.
Track each institution's strategic priorities throughout the year and escalate stalled progress or risks.
Identify and design improvements to LI's operating systems and templates (discovery process, communications cadence, reporting formats) in partnership with the VP.
Institution & Partner Liaison

Field routine questions and troubleshoot logistics directly.
Spot opportunities raised by campus partners and elevate them to the VP
Cross-Team Coordination & Communication
Manage meeting cadence and information flow among the VP, consulting, partnerships, and impact teams
Maintain and organize program materials, including discovery reports, session decks, PLC, and coaching resources
Model clear, professional communication in every touchpoint with institutional partners
Data Tracking & Reporting
Track Pillar-specific progress and coaching-call reflections across the cohort.
Synthesize cohort-wide data into formats leaders can act on, including progress dashboards, insights reports, and summaries.

An experienced program manager. You bring 5+ years of program or project management experience, ideally spanning cross-functional or partner-facing work in education, consulting, or nonprofit settings.

If so, Opencast could be the place for you. We’re a growing tech consultancy that creates user-centred solutions with purpose for our clients in government, healthcare and purpose-driven businesses. As an Agile Delivery Manager, you’ll tackle challenges and guide teams, adding structure, assurance and energy to complex projects that make a difference to millions of people in the UK.

You’ll collaborate with the product manager and team to lead the delivery of services and products that deliver our clients’ strategic outcomes. You'll facilitate people’s work in roles spanning design, development, and research, playing a key leadership role in multidisciplinary agile teams.

We are unable to progress applications from candidates who do not meet these requirements.

Projektleiter / Ingenieur Brandschutz 80–100% \| Brandschutzfachmann/\-frau, Brandschutzexperte oder Quereinstieg
Du kennst den Brandschutz bereits – oder möchtest ihn zu deinem neuen Fachgebiet machen?
Brandschutz ist heute weit mehr als das Anwenden von Vorschriften. Gute Lösungen entstehen dort, wo Architektur, Gebäudetechnik, Sicherheit, Wirtschaftlichkeit und die Anforderungen der Bauherrschaft zusammenkommen.
Genau hier arbeiten wir bei AFC.
Wir begleiten einige der anspruchsvollsten Bauprojekte der Schweiz und entwickeln Brandschutzlösungen für Neubauten, Umbauten und komplexe Bestandsgebäude. Dabei kombinieren wir klassische Brandschutzplanung mit ingenieurmässigen Nachweisen, Simulationen, Qualitätssicherung und integralen Tests.
Für unser Brandschutzteam suchen wir Persönlichkeiten, die Verantwortung übernehmen und sich fachlich weiterentwickeln möchten.
Ob du bereits Brandschutzexperte oder Brandschutzfachmann/\-frau bist oder als Architekt bzw. Ingenieur neu in den Brandschutz einsteigen möchtest: Entscheidend sind für uns dein technisches Verständnis, deine Motivation und dein Wille, gute Lösungen zu entwickeln.
Das kannst du bei uns bewegen
Du arbeitest an anspruchsvollen Brandschutzprojekten von der ersten Idee bis zur Inbetriebnahme.
Je nach Erfahrung und Ausbildungsstand übernimmst du schrittweise mehr Verantwortung:
Du entwickelst Brandschutzkonzepte für Neu\- und Umbauten und suchst gemeinsam mit Bauherrschaften, Architekt und Fachplanenden nach praktikablen und wirtschaftlichen Lösungen.
Du berätst unsere Auftraggeber und vertrittst Projekte gegenüber Behörden und weiteren Projektbeteiligten.
Du bearbeitest Fragestellungen des baulichen, technischen und organisatorischen Brandschutzes.
Du begleitest Projekte durch Planung und Realisierung, führst Qualitätskontrollen auf Baustellen durch und unterstützt bei Abnahmen und Inbetriebnahmen.
Mit wachsender Erfahrung leitest du deine Projekte selbstständig und verantwortest Qualität, Termine und Kosten. Wenn dich ingenieurmässiger Brandschutz interessiert, kannst du dich bei AFC auch mit leistungs\- und risikobasierten Nachweisen, Entrauchung, Evakuation, Simulationen, Brandfallsteuerungen oder Integralen Tests vertieft beschäftigen.
Drei Wege zu AFC
Du bist Brandschutzexperte VKF
Du verfügst bereits über umfassende Erfahrung und möchtest anspruchsvolle Projekte selbstständig führen. Bei AFC erhältst du den Raum, komplexe Aufgaben zu übernehmen, Kunden zu beraten und deine fachliche Erfahrung in einem starken Brandschutzteam einzubringen und weiterzuentwickeln.
Du bist Brandschutzfachmann/\-frau VKF
Du möchtest den nächsten Schritt machen und zunehmend grössere und komplexere Projekte verantworten. Wir unterstützen dich fachlich und organisatorisch auf deinem weiteren Weg – bei Interesse bis zur Qualifikation als Brandschutzexperte.
Du kommst aus Architektur oder Ingenieurwesen
Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium in Architektur, Bauingenieurwesen, Holzbau, HLK, Gebäudetechnik oder einer vergleichbaren technischen Fachrichtung und möchtest dich beruflich neu orientieren?
Dann bist du ausdrücklich willkommen.
Du musst noch kein Brandschutzprofi sein. Was wir erwarten, sind ein solides Verständnis für Gebäude und Technik, analytisches Denken und eine hohe Motivation, dich intensiv in den Brandschutz einzuarbeiten.
Dein Fachwissen bleibt. Dein Fachgebiet wird neu.
Nutze die Chance für einen beruflichen Neustart in einem zukunftsorientierten Fachgebiet und werde Teil unseres Teams. Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen. jpid904f4d8jm jit0936jm jiy26jm

Nous aidons les clients à évaluer la performance opérationnelle avant la signature, à identifier et quantifier les opportunités de création de valeur, et à gérer les complexités des acquisitions, cessions et scissions.

Chez Deloitte, nous collaborons étroitement avec nos collègues des services transactionnels, des évaluations et de la finance d'entreprise pour garantir une approche fluide et axée sur la valeur des transactions.
**Comment vous ferez la différence**
Vous travaillerez avec des équipes de direction d-entreprises, des investisseurs en capital-investissement et des professionnels des fusions-acquisitions pour identifier et réaliser la valeur issue des transactions M&A. Vous aiderez à façonner la réflexion stratégique, à traiter les enjeux critiques de performance et à mobiliser l-ensemble des compétences de Deloitte pour maximiser la valeur des transactions.
En tant que membre d-une équipe dédiée de spécialistes M&A, vous fournirez des conseils en due diligence opérationnelle en reliant la performance financière, les capacités opérationnelles et l-ambition stratégique. Votre travail portera sur la croissance des revenus et la réduction des coûts à travers le coût des marchandises vendues (COGS) et les frais généraux, administratifs et commerciaux (SG&A), que ce soit par des opportunités d-amélioration autonome ou des synergies transactionnelles.

* Une expérience et une connaissance dans une ou plusieurs des industries suivantes : Énergie, Ressources & Industriels ; Consommation ; Sciences de la vie & Santé ; ou Technologie, Médias & Télécommunications ;
* Excellentes compétences analytiques et de résolution de problèmes, avec la capacité de décomposer des enjeux complexes, d-identifier les causes profondes et de recommander des solutions actionnables ; et
* Une maîtrise professionnelle complète de l-anglais ; la maîtrise de l-allemand, idéalement incluant l-allemand suisse, est fortement souhaitée.
